<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **101** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited), getOverlayRepo (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via applyRegistryWriteThrough (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited), ensureObjectStorage (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 00110fd768efd225285dc2d83e8ebd9619fb5b60` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `df15ab8302918b497686cc22cb72b3a3703e7d1b` — the merge of head `92307330a4af57f6f14742254dee68fd54f0469b` into base `00110fd768efd225285dc2d83e8ebd9619fb5b60`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin df15ab8302918b497686cc22cb72b3a3703e7d1b && git checkout df15ab8302918b497686cc22cb72b3a3703e7d1b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 00110fd768efd225285dc2d83e8ebd9619fb5b60 92307330a4af57f6f14742254dee68fd54f0469b && git checkout -B drift-repro 00110fd768efd225285dc2d83e8ebd9619fb5b60 && git merge --no-ff 92307330a4af57f6f14742254dee68fd54f0469b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 00110fd768efd225285dc2d83e8ebd9619fb5b60
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 00110fd768efd225285dc2d83e8ebd9619fb5b60` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXGvw43spR79ztEvWt

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8ee295be6910e5380c96c95aed5b9dee0258973a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-operator-field-type-fit.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/destructive-still-shown-by.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts

First full review of PR #35239 (card #35147), net diff against merge base `ec227fc7b1`. Read: the card and its six comments (claim 6983829040, amendment 6987803352, dev reports 6987756263 and 6988813376), the PR body and its comments, the diff, and the check-runs on the head. The dev reports were read as accounts and checked against the tree. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `@objectstack/lint` (the three judges), `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`, `filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts`, the objectql text-operator door, `error-response.ts`, `thrown-http-error.ts`, `mcp-authoring.ts`, `view.zod.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `@objectstack/spec/api` gains `DestructiveChangeIssueSchema` and `FieldStillShownBySchema` with their author and parsed aliases. Right: the api-surface, declaration-map, export-origins, json-schema manifest and authorable-surface rows (9) all moved with them. Both are plain `z.object`, every new key is optional except the three the producer always writes, so no existing answer stops parsing.
- The wire answer widens: each `field_removed` and `field_type_change` entry of the `409 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` `issues[]` may carry `stillShownBy`, and its `message` gains a trailing sentence when items are named. Right, and additive. The five `code` values the describe lists are exactly the five `detectDestructiveObjectChanges` emits (`protocol-write-face.ts:186-305`); `withNullMasterRowCounts` rewrites `message` only, so the three declared keys plus `stillShownBy` are the whole entry.
- The three doors relay `err.issues` untouched, as the schema docblock says, and none is in the diff: REST flat body `issues` (`rest/src/error-response.ts:640`), the shared thrown-error rule `details.issues` (`types/src/thrown-http-error.ts:350-359`), the MCP draft door `error.issues` (`runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts:568-569, 883-884`). Right.
- `@objectstack/spec/data` gains `filterOperatorFieldTypeFit`, `FILTER_OPERATOR_FIELD_TYPE_FIT`, three types, and `dollarFilterOperatorOf`. Right: all six are in `api-surface/data.json`. `dollarFilterOperatorOf` is a new public export. It is needed (the lowering table `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` and `astOperatorLowering` are module-private, and `canonicalAstOperator` answers the infix spelling, not the `$` one), and it is declared in the amendment and in the changeset prose.
- No accept-set narrows. No authorable metadata key is added: the 9 authorable-surface rows are response-schema rows.
- `packages/metadata-protocol` exports nothing new from its entry; `destructive-still-shown-by.ts` is internal. `getMetaItems` joins the `saveMetaItemUnaudited` host pick. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening: the DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE answer gains stillShownBy; a new exported operator-fit table)` matches the diff. The line does not name `dollarFilterOperatorOf`; the changeset prose does. Accepted.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` matches `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` (+9 rows).
- `@objectstack/spec: minor` is right for new exports and two new schemas. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` is accepted: its entry points are unchanged and the wire widening is carried by the spec bump.
- `Skills-docs: none` holds: no file under `skills/` names `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE`, `field_removed` or `field_type_change`.
- The PR body and the changeset carry the same three declaration lines. `Check Changeset` newest run on the head (135063047492) is success; the earlier failure (135049482886) read the body before it was patched.
- Changeset prose against the code: each sentence holds, with three loose ones recorded as N8.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev Q1, the wiring in `protocol-save.ts`: answered A by the seat in 6987803352. The tree agrees: the 409 is thrown at `protocol-save.ts`, the wiring is one call plus the host pick, and `protocol-write-face.ts` is untouched.
- Dev Q2, the declaration: answered by the amendment, landed in the changeset at this head and in the live PR body.
- Dev note, `operatorsForFieldType` in `ui/packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx`: the note holds. It selects which operators a dropdown draws (buckets by field type, opt-in gate, nullness pair). It refuses nothing and no server door reads it, so it is not the second judge the card forbids. It is still a second operator-by-type table, and it disagrees with the judgement in both directions by design. The dev noted it with no carrier; a follow-up card to point it at `filterOperatorFieldTypeFit` is the seat's to file or decline.
- Dev note, comparand doors not judged on a type change: stated in the describe and in the module header. Accepted as scope.
- Dev account, red leg and ablation: not re-run (read-only). Read against the test file: the five removal cases depend on the wiring and the type-change case on the fit verdict, so both accounts are plausible. What the pins do not hold, for the lane seat:
  - absent versus `[]`: no case makes a listing fail or a judge throw, so the "not computed" half of the contract is unpinned;
  - `via`: no dataset or dashboard fixture, so the one step the module adds beyond the lint judges is unpinned;
  - the served ViewItem shape (`viewKind` plus `config`), which is what `getMetaItems('view')` serves for a code-registered view, is not a fixture. The form fixture is a root-`sections` record with no `viewKind`;
  - the listing bound is "at most 2 view reads" and, by the dev's own account, passes with no reads;
  - the REST flat `issues` leg has no case here. The case named "the HTTP doors" reads `resolveThrownHttpError`, which answers `details.issues`. The only REST assertion is the dogfood one below.
- Dogfood assertion (`meta-object-unstored-field-removal.dogfood.test.ts` now expects `stillShownBy: []`): NOT MEASURED. The dev did not run it, and on this head the dogfood shards are skipped (`Dogfood Regression Gate` 135049825788 concluded success with its matrix leg 135049827698 skipped). By reading, `[]` is the expected answer for a field of a runtime-saved object in an otherwise empty app. It hides nothing in the diff, but it is also the only case that would show the real boot producing the key at all. The lane seat should have it run once before landing.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The new code reads no record and materialises no id. It reads one served listing per metadata type through `getMetaItems`, in parallel, and judges metadata bodies in process; there is no SQL form of that judgement.
- Reads: confirmed against the code. Nothing is read unless a `field_removed` or `field_type_change` finding exists; views alone for a type change, seven listings for a removal; no per-item read. `getMetaItems` is the served (redacted) read, which is the right one for a door that answers a caller.
- Check-runs on the head at reading: 59 success, 12 skipped, 1 superseded failure (`Check Changeset`, above), and `Test Core (9/10)` (135050867441) still in progress. The other nine Test Core shards, TypeScript Type Check and Lint & Repo Gates are success. This record does not cover shard 9: the seat reads its conclusion before landing.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, against `destructive-still-shown-by.ts`.

S1 (should-fix) — the `stillShownBy` and `where` describes do not match what the served `view` listing can produce. `getMetaItems('view')` never serves an aggregated container: `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts:990-992` filters every item `isAggregatedViewContainer` claims (no `viewKind`, and a `list`, `form`, `listViews` or `formViews`), and stored containers are expanded into ViewItems first. So the items the module reads are ViewItems (`viewKind` plus `config`), flattened list overlays, and bare records. Three consequences:
  - The type-change sentence names "a view's own `filter`, its `list` view's and each `listViews` entry's". The code reads four sites: the record, `config`, `list` and `listViews.*` (`destructive-still-shown-by.ts:290-295`). `config` is the site of the canonical served shape and is not described. `list` and `listViews.*`, and the `isContainer` name fallback, cannot be reached from a served listing.
  - The `where` examples `listViews.all.columns[1]` and `formViews.edit.sections[0].fields[2]` are container paths. The paths a client will see are `config.columns[1]`, `config.sections[0].fields[2]` or `columns[1]`.
  - A list view's `userFilters.tabs[].filter` is a list-view filter the type-change half does not judge. It is in neither the judged list nor the "not judged" list, which names only datasets, dashboards, reports and flows.
  The module's first paragraph calls this describe "the contract this module computes", and the changeset says it "states exactly what is and is not seen". Fix: describe the sites the served listing can present (`filter`, `config.filter`), correct the examples, name tab filters as not judged, and either remove the two unreachable rungs or say why they stay. The removal half is unaffected: it takes its positions from the lint judges, which read both the ViewItem `config` rung and the flattened overlay.

Otherwise the schema holds. `type` lists exactly the seven types `COLLECTIONS` maps. `via` is set only on a dashboard entry. `operator` is set only by the type-change half. Absent versus `[]` is as described for an unreadable listing.

`packages/spec/src/data/filter-operator-field-type-fit.ts`.

Holds as the one judgement. Its single row references `TEXT_FILTER_OPERATORS` and `textOperatorDoorVerdict`; the known-operator set is the union of `FILTER_OPERATORS` and `TEXT_FILTER_OPERATORS`. No operator and no field type is re-listed. I read the other declared-type modules in `packages/spec/src/data` (number, boolean, string-stored and temporal comparand doors, `$empty`, cross-field class, dotted head): each judges a comparand, an expansion or a column pair, none an operator class by field type, so one row is the right count today. Per field type the answer is the engine door's own: `packages/objectql/src/text-operator-declared-type-door.ts` refuses exactly when `textOperatorDoorVerdict` answers `door-refusal`, on an undotted key, which is the condition the type-change walker applies (bare field name). No second judge exists in `packages/lint`, `packages/rest`, `packages/mcp` or `packages/metadata-protocol`.

`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`.

`dollarFilterOperatorOf` folds through `astOperatorLowering`, the same table `canonicalAstOperator` reads, and its docblock states the two direction-erasing pairs and that a `$` spelling is returned as written. Every `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` member and every `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` key lowers. The barrel line is in the right place. Holds.

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/destructive-still-shown-by.ts`, tried against false positives, false negatives and cost.

- False positive: none found. Both runs judge the same stack with the saved object last, so paths and indexes are stable, and a finding both runs share cancels. That includes every finding caused by what the stand-in body lacks (system columns, absent collections such as actions or apps). Each removed field is taken out alone against a baseline that restores all of them, so one field's findings are not charged to another.
- False negative: bounded by the judges, as the describe says. Rules for each claimed type are in the suite the code calls (list views, object field lists, related lists, page bindings, report and chart bindings, dataset references, flow template paths and node writes, form layout, widget bindings), and their paths are `collection[index]…`, which the path pattern reads. Not seen, and consistent with the describe: expressions inside formulas and predicates, and a removal that adds to a finding already present at the same rule and path.
- Cost: listings as stated in ③. See N5.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract as landed):

- N1 — `withStillShownBy` is called inside the `try` whose `catch` reads every throw other than `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` as "skip the safety check" (`protocol-save.ts`, the catch after the throw). The module catches a failed listing and a throwing judge itself, and I found no remaining throw path. A later edit that throws there would land a destructive save without its 409. Computing the items outside that `try`, or catching at the call, removes the dependency.
- N2 — three producer behaviours the describes do not state: `where` holds the literal `(root)` when a finding sits on the item itself; one item can appear in more than one entry (a dashboard directly and once per `via` dataset, a view once per unfit operator); `stillShownBy` is also absent when a judge throws or the retyped field's new definition has no readable `type`.
- N3 — the stand-in object is named `str(next.name) ?? objectName`, while the served copy is removed by `objectName`. A body whose `name` differs from the address would be judged under the body's name and answer `[]`. I did not establish whether the save refuses such a body earlier. Naming the stand-in by `objectName` closes it either way.
- N4 — entries are keyed `type:name:via`. Two served items of one type and name in different packages merge into one entry, and the entry carries no package.
- N5 — a removal runs the three judges over the whole served stack once per removed field plus once. That is fine for the usual one field. It is unbounded in the number of removed fields on one save, synchronous, and not measured.
- N6 — `fits` means "no operator-class door refuses", not "the filter is served". A field retyped to `formula` has every filter refused by the unmaterializable-field door (`INVALID_FIELD`), and the judgement answers `fits` or `unjudged`. The text door's own header says this; the new module header and the `stillShownBy` describe do not.
- N7 — the module declares its own `DestructiveFinding` instead of reading `DestructiveChangeIssue`, and no test parses a produced finding through `DestructiveChangeIssueSchema`. The schema is the wire shape by reading, not by a pin.
- N8 — changeset prose: "`dollarFilterOperatorOf(op)` lowers any operator spelling to its `$` form" (a `$` spelling is returned unchecked and an unknown one answers `undefined`); "the finding's message names the same items" (the first five, then a count); "the MCP draft door (`issues`)" (it is `error.issues`).

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35147-destructive-still-shown-by`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbXGvw43spR79ztEvWt`

**VERDICT: PASS**

repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXGvw43spR79ztEvWt

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `92307330a4af57f6f14742254dee68fd54f0469b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-operator-field-type-fit.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/destructive-still-shown-by.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts

Delta review of `8ee295be6910e5380c96c95aed5b9dee0258973a..92307330a4af57f6f14742254dee68fd54f0469b`, following record 6989169773 (PASS with S1 open, nits N1 to N8). The delta holds three commits of this PR (`1b46817fa4`, `abe7996ad3`, `d439001c9f`), the merge `be571b4077` of `main` `b02484e13a`, and the regeneration `92307330a4`. Only this PR's own changes are judged. Read: the card and its comments (dev report 6992236035 as an account, checked against the tree), the live PR body, the delta, the net diff against `b02484e13a`, and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`, `protocol-view-normalization.ts`, `view.zod.ts`, `filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts`, `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`, `build-probes.ts`, `metadata-diagnostics.ts`. In the three `hits` files under `packages/spec/src/data` the delta changes nothing; the earlier judgement stands.

### ① Derived judgments

- No new export and no accept-set change in the delta. In `protocol.zod.ts` the PR's own delta is describe text on `FieldStillShownBySchema.name`, `.where`, on `DestructiveChangeIssueSchema.stillShownBy`, and one docblock word (`error.issues`). The `AiConversationMessageSchema` hunk in the same range is #35240, from the merge, and is not judged.
- The wire answer changes in one place: a `field_type_change` finding now also names a rule under `userFilters.tabs[].filter` (of a view item's `config` or of a flattened overlay), and no longer reads `list` or `listViews.*`. Right: the first is additive on an optional key, the second removes sites the served listing cannot present, so no served answer loses an entry.
- Generated files, net against `main` `b02484e13a`: they carry this PR's rows and nothing else. `api-surface/api.json` +6, `api-surface/data.json` +6, `authorable-surface/api.json` +9, `declaration-map/api.json` +4, `export-origins` +6 and +6, `json-schema.manifest/api.json` +2, the reference index 1698 to 1700 schemas, and `protocol.mdx` with the two new sections carrying the new describe text. No row contradicts the source. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains the two new test files' `findOne` rows.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening: the DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE answer gains stillShownBy; a new exported operator-fit table)` still matches the diff.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` still matches `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` (+9 rows against `main`).
- `@objectstack/spec: minor` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` are unchanged and still right: the delta adds no export and changes no entry point.
- `Skills-docs: none` is unchanged and still holds.
- The live PR body and the changeset carry the same three declaration lines. `Check Changeset` on the head is success (135147992347 and 135149626707).
- Changeset prose against the code, sentence by sentence: holds. The served paths, the three filter sites, "names the first five items and counts the rest" (`PROSE_CAP = 5`), `error.issues`, the absent cases and the `dollarFilterOperatorOf` sentence are each true of the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev report carries no open question. Its deviations: the dogfood file ran at the pre-merge implementation, not on the merged head. Accepted as an account: the merge brought no change to the destructive path. It is still NOT MEASURED by CI: `Dogfood Regression Gate` (135148324459) concluded success with its matrix leg skipped, as on the previous head.
- L1 point, the lint root on the save path: taken. `destructive-still-shown-by.ts` holds no static import of `@objectstack/lint`; the only import is `await import('@objectstack/lint')` inside `loadJudges`, reached only when a `field_removed` finding exists. A failed load answers `undefined`, `removalSurfaces` is not called, and each `field_removed` finding is returned without the key. A `field_type_change` finding in the same save is still computed, which is right: it needs no judge. The module header's reason is true: `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts` exports the gate functions and `closureDependencyRemedy` only, none of the three judges, and `build-probes.ts:470` and `metadata-diagnostics.ts:552, 663` load the root the same lazy way. The served `view` read already loads the root lazily for its diagnostics, so this adds no new load to a save that reaches a view listing.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The delta adds no read. The tab-filter walk reads the `view` listing the type-change half already held; no id is materialised and no record is read.
- Red leg and N1 ablation: not re-run (read-only). Read against the tests, both accounts are consistent. On `8ee295be69` the two lint-entry cases fail on the static import, the tab-filter case fails because the walker read no `userFilters`, and the throw case fails because the enclosing catch swallowed the throw and the save went on.
